title: Add todo to utilz
objective: Add a `utilz todo` utility: a standalone, single-file manager for a plain-text `todo.md` with DOING / TODO / DONE buckets, positional item numbers, and history sweep/purge subcommands. It is a fork of Intent's `intent todo`, made independent of steel threads -- the `todo.md` is the source of truth rather than a projection.
context: Factored out of `intent todo` so a plain, project-agnostic todo file can be managed anywhere (cwd `./todo.md` or a global `-g` file). Two hard constraints carry over from Intent: the `todo.md` file format stays mutually compatible (same `## DOING/TODO/DONE:<watermark>` headings, same `[ ]/[-]/[x]` glyphs), and the command names stay identical to `intent todo` wherever the standalone context allows. The full design, including the projection-vs-source-of-truth fork and the divergences (frontmatter, item numbers, no GFM dash), is in `design.md`.

wps.title: utilz todo <-> intent todo mutual guard (utilz side)
wps.objective: Make `utilz todo` and `intent todo` mutually non-clobbering across the shared `todo.md` format. `utilz todo` stamps a `generator: utilz todo` ownership marker on every write, and refuses to overwrite a file owned by a different generator (eg `intent todo`) -- but only when Intent is actually present, so utilz stays a zero-dependency standalone tool that runs silently and never fails anywhere Intent isn't. This is the utilz half of the symmetric contract Intent shipped in 2.16.1 (`bin/intent_todo:guard_foreign_todo`).
wps.body:
## Deliverables

- Stamp `generator: utilz todo` into the frontmatter emitted by the single writer (`write_file`), alongside `title:` / `history:`. Unconditional -- independent of Intent's presence.
- A `guard_foreign_todo` seam mirroring Intent's, called at the top of `write_file`: proceed silently when the file is absent, has no frontmatter, has frontmatter without a `generator:` (utilz's own pre-marker `title:`/`history:` file), or is marked `generator: utilz todo`; otherwise the file is foreign.
- Intent-aware gating on the foreign branch only: refuse (clear error + non-zero exit) only when BOTH `command -v intent` succeeds AND the **target file's own directory tree** contains a valid Intent project (`intent/.config/config.json`, walking upward from `dirname($TODO_FILE)`). Deliberately anchored on the file, not cwd (this diverges from Intent's cwd-based `find_project_root` on purpose): the guard's question is "does the file I'm about to overwrite belong to an Intent project?", so pointing `--file` at another project's `intent/todo.md` from outside still triggers it. Otherwise proceed and re-stamp as utilz. No emissions when Intent is absent.
- Default-path creation guard (follow-up): refuse to CREATE a fresh default `./todo.md` inside an Intent project (same `_intent_present` + `_in_intent_project` gates, plus a `DEFAULT_PATH` flag). Closes the first-use gap where a bare `utilz todo` littered a `todo.md` in an Intent project; explicit `--file`/`-g`, existing utilz files, read-only queries, and non-Intent dirs are unaffected.
- BATS coverage in `opt/todo/test/todo.bats`: stamp present; foreign-refusal inside an Intent project (with a stubbed `intent` on PATH); foreign-proceed outside a project; own / legacy / fresh pass-through; default-path creation refused in an Intent project; existing utilz file in a project still works.
- Docs: the ownership contract noted in `help/todo.md` and `opt/todo/README.md`.

## Dependencies

- Builds on WP-01..07 (the shipped `todo` utility). No new WP dependencies.
- Mirrors the Intent-side guard in Intent 2.16.1 (`bin/intent_todo`), but takes **no runtime dependency on Intent** -- utilz only reads the target file's frontmatter, plus a silent `command -v intent` and an upward `intent/.config/config.json` check.

criteria.text: A fresh `list` (no file present) creates `todo.md` from the template: YAML frontmatter with `title: "# TODO"` and `history: _history/YYYYMMDD-done.md`, the `# TODO` H1, and the three buckets `## DOING`, `## TODO`, `## DONE:<ISO-8601-UTC>`, empty buckets shown as `_(none)_`.
`add <text>` appends the item to the bottom of TODO with `[ ]`; `add --top <text>` prepends it to the top of TODO.
Item numbers are global and positional in file order (DOING, TODO, DONE), zero-padded to the max width present (1--9 -> `N`, 10--99 -> `NN`), rendered as `<num>:[<glyph>] <text>`.
File-location precedence: `--file <path>` wins; `-g`/`--global` resolves `${XDG_CONFIG_HOME:-$HOME/.config}/utilz/todo/todo.md`; default is `./todo.md`; `--file` with `-g` errors non-zero.
Writes are atomic (temp + `mv`) and normalization is idempotent: running the write path twice yields a byte-identical file.
`start <id>` moves the item to DOING as `[-]` (bottom by default, top with `--top`).
`done <id>` moves the item to DONE as `[x]`, prepended so the newest completion is at the top of DONE.
`notdone <id>` moves the item to TODO as `[ ]`.
`toggle <id>` flips done <-> not-done from the item's current glyph.
An unknown `<id>` errors with a clear message and non-zero exit (no silent no-op).
`next` prints the next open item (DOING first, then TODO); `next <n>` prints the next `n`; default 1.
`doing`, `todo`, and bare `done` print their respective buckets.
`count` prints the item count per bucket.

`done --prune` prepends the DONE block to the history file (path from frontmatter `history:`, `YYYYMMDD` expanded to today UTC, resolved relative to the todo.md directory, dirs created), strips the positional number to `[x] <text>`, removes the items from `todo.md`, and stamps `## DONE:<now-UTC>`.
`done --flush` clears the DONE bucket without archiving; it is confirm-guarded and proceeds non-interactively with `--force`/`--just-do-it`.
A custom `history:` pattern in frontmatter is honoured (archive lands at the custom path).
`sync` reconciles glyph vs section with glyph authoritative: an item marked `[x]` under `## TODO` relocates to the top of DONE; a `[ ]`/`[-]` under `## DONE` relocates out to TODO/DOING.
`sync` tolerates hand-entered lines -- missing number, stray leading `- `, `[x]foo` with no space -- normalizing and renumbering them.
`sync` warns on stderr for an unrecognizable non-blank line under a bucket and preserves it (never silently dropped).
`update` is an alias that runs `sync`.
`edit` opens the resolved file in `$VISUAL` (else `$EDITOR`, else `vi`) and runs `sync` on exit; with none resolvable it errors clearly.
`--json` emits a valid object `{title, doing[], todo[], done[], done_watermark}` parseable by `jq`.
`opt/todo/todo.yaml` carries an `integration:` block so the Emacs bridge lists `todo`.
`opt/todo/README.md` and `help/todo.md` document every verb and option.
`utilz doctor` and `utilz list` pass with `todo` registered and its deps declared in YAML.

state.evidence: `utilz doctor` (todo properly configured; only pre-existing PATH warning) + `utilz list` shows todo

criteria.text: Every `todo.md` utilz writes carries `generator: utilz todo` in its YAML frontmatter (alongside `title:`/`history:`); the stamp is unconditional -- independent of whether Intent is installed or the file is in an Intent project.

On a mutating command whose target file's frontmatter `generator:` names a different tool (eg `intent todo`), utilz refuses with a clear error and non-zero exit -- but only when BOTH `command -v intent` succeeds AND the file's own directory tree contains a valid Intent project (`intent/.config/config.json`, walking upward from the file's directory). On refusal the file is left byte-unchanged and no history file is created.

A file safe to write is written without error and gains the marker: no frontmatter (legacy Intent / fresh), frontmatter without a `generator:` (utilz's pre-marker `title:`/`history:` file), or `generator: utilz todo` (utilz's own). A foreign-marked file that is NOT inside an Intent project is taken over and re-stamped `generator: utilz todo`.

With Intent absent, utilz never fails or emits an Intent-related message on account of the guard, even for a foreign-marked file inside an Intent project tree (the `command -v intent` gate short-circuits to proceed).

With its DEFAULT path (no `--file`/`-g`) and no `./todo.md` present yet, utilz refuses to CREATE a new file inside an Intent project (Intent installed AND cwd's tree contains `intent/.config/config.json`), directing the user to `intent todo` or `--file`/`-g`; the file is not created and exit is non-zero. Unaffected (all proceed): explicit `--file`/`-g`, an already-existing utilz `./todo.md`, read-only queries that never write, non-Intent directories, and Intent-absent.
